basis: The Commission states that the law on free movement and residence of EU citizens, in force since March 2026, aims to align with the acquis on the rights of workers, and the government states that it gives EU citizens equal treatment with nationals.
The 2025 report presents the July 2025 law, under access to the labour market, as giving EU citizens a regime different from other third-country nationals.
The draft amendment to the employment law is stated to guarantee the rights of unemployed EU citizens and to remove the citizenship condition for staff of private employment agencies.
The government states that the amendment to Government Decision No. 1276/2018 is to give EU citizens access to the employment agency's services and active measures.
The government states that several ministries are adjusting secondary legislation following Law No. 200/2025, including to give EU citizens and their family members access to education and training.
The government states that the amendment is to remove gaps that would prevent Member State citizens' access to service housing.
The planned training is stated to ensure equal treatment of EU citizens and their family members exercising their rights under Law No. 200/2025.
The amendments, applicable from March 2026, entitle EU citizens and their family members holding a residence card to the employment agency's services and measures.
The government states that the 2023 amendments let EU citizens work for 90 days in any 180 without a residence permit for work.
The Commission states that the amendments in force from January 2024 allow EU citizens to work in Moldova without a work permit.
The government states that under Law No. 200/2025 EU citizens need no work authorisation or residence permit for employment, only a residence card for stays over 90 days.
The Commission links the standard operating procedure of March 2026 to applications by EU citizens for the new residence documents.
The draft law is stated to separate the regime for third-country nationals from the regime for EU citizens and their family members.
The government states that the Ministry of Internal Affairs will set how arriving Member State citizens are registered, which requires revising its secondary legislation.
The Commission reports a Labour Migration and EURES department with a designated officer in the employment agency's structure from January 2025, responsible for preparatory work for EURES.
The government states that the measure ensures interoperability between the agency's Labour Market information system and the EURES platform.
The Commission reports the agency's new integrated information system, aimed at fully digitalised services, and the government says it will also provide interoperability with EESSI.
The draft orders set technical standards and formats for interoperability between the national information system and EURES.
The government lists training of agency staff on the EURES portal and network among the measures to strengthen the agency's capacity for EURES.
The measure sets minimum requirements for processing personal data in the data exchange with EURES.
The correlation tables map national skills, competences and occupations to the European classification used by EURES.
The measure revises job descriptions on the angajat.md portal to meet EURES criteria.
The draft law sets the conditions for admission and paid work of foreigners and their equal treatment with nationals in working conditions.
The draft amendment is stated to give other categories of foreign citizens, including those staying for work or under temporary protection, access to employment services.
The employment agency's own reports describe its support to displaced persons from Ukraine who wish to work in Moldova.

The migration inspectorate states that the proposed amendments are to remove problems in the foreigners, integration and state fee laws identified by the working group on stimulating the labour market.
The draft amendment regulates the work of certain categories of foreigners and how they submit documents at the One-Stop Shop.
The migration inspectorate reports work with the ICT companies' association on improving the regulatory framework for foreign IT specialists.
The government cites the 2024 cooperation agreement between the migration inspectorate and the labour inspectorate in reply to the comment on separating labour inspection from immigration control.
The 2023 report states that the regulation obliges contracting authorities to carry out most low-value procurement through the State Registry of Public Procurement information system.
The government states that the public services portal is to be reconfigured to fulfil the role of point of single contact.
The government lists the functionality and interoperability of the National Register of Qualifications with the Europass database among actions on recognising qualifications.
The regulator links the 2024 and 2025 spectrum competitions to wider coverage and to the roll-out of 5G networks.
The Implementation Programme 2025-2027 includes developing electronic communications networks in the identified white areas.
The regulator states that the World Bank project aims to extend high-speed broadband access and has mapped uncovered white zones.
The standard licence conditions oblige holders of 700 MHz and 800 MHz licences to provide cumulative mobile broadband coverage.
Freedom House reports the regulator's preparatory process to license the frequency bands needed for 5G networks.
The Commission states that the 2024 law aims to align Moldova's legislation with the GDPR, and in 2026 that it entered into force.
The 2026 report states that the law on personal data processed for crime prevention aligns with the Law Enforcement Directive.
The 2026 report records ratification of the second protocol to Convention 108, which the 2025 report recommended.
The draft order on standard contractual clauses answers the Commission's 2025 and 2026 calls to implement EU standards on such clauses.
The 2023 report describes the revision of national laws for harmonisation with the data protection law, pending since 2020.
The draft law is stated to amend Law No. 142/2018 to transpose the Interoperable Europe Act.
The government states that the priority is aligning the national interoperability framework with the European Interoperability Framework.
The e-Government Agency states that the Code of Contraventions now sanctions breaches of the data exchange law, including unjustified refusal to provide data through the platform.
The e-Government Agency states that the amendment expressly lays down the obligation to connect to the interoperability platform and take part in data exchange.
The Reform Agenda step requires asset declarations to go through the new e-Integrity system, with interoperability with other platforms ensured through MConnect.
The Digital Transformation Strategy states that interoperability between state registers will reduce the data repeatedly requested from citizens.
The government plans to transpose the EU Chips Act by the end of 2026.
The government states that implementing the semiconductor acquis requires a new principal consultant post in the economy ministry.
The 2023 report states that data exchange through MConnect enabled the Central Electoral Commission to check political party financing more effectively.
The Court of Accounts follow-up audit gives the legal conditions for data exchange between SIERUSS and SIA REA as the impact of the actions taken, including the SIERUSS Concept.
The regulator states that Moldtelecom's 4G coverage expanded thanks to the sub-1 GHz spectrum awarded in the competitions.
The regulator states that the spectrum award contributes to network capacity, high-speed broadband and the national roll-out of 5G.
The Commission's assessment for the third Reform and Growth Facility release states that the alignment, including Law No. 72/2025, facilitates the roll-out of higher speed and affordable networks.
